database_summary: This is a motorsport (Formula 1-style) dataset containing descriptive dimension tables (circuits, drivers, constructors, seasons, status, short name lookups, ext summary tables) and event/measurement fact tables (races, results, sprint_results, qualifying, lap_times, lap_times_ext, pit_stops, lap_positions, retirements). There are also standings/history tables (driver_standings, constructor_standings, constructor_results) and helper tables for team/driver ranks, drives and livery/time ranges. Primary keys are explicit in many base tables; several *_ext tables duplicate base data with added summary columns. Join keys are predominantly race_id, driver_id, constructor_id and circuit_id. Many joins (results ↔ lap_times ↔ lap_positions ↔ pit_stops) can multiply rows because those fact tables are at different granularities (race-driver-lap vs race-driver vs race). Use caution when joining standings or aggregate stats to results because they represent snapshots per race or evolving championship state.

accepted.name: race_basic
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  race_id,
  year,
  round,
  circuit_id,
  name,
  date,
  time,
  url,
  fp1_date,
  fp1_time,
  fp2_date,
  fp2_time,
  fp3_date,
  fp3_time,
  quali_date,
  quali_time,
  sprint_date,
  sprint_time,
  CAST(date AS TEXT) AS date_text
FROM races
accepted.description: Normalized projection of races with canonical date/time fields and essential identifiers. Use this to join race metadata to results, lap times, pit stops, and standings. Keeps original column names and exposes a derived epoch_date for easy time-based ordering. | Use for: List races in a year or range; Join race metadata to results, lap_times, pit_stops; Filter races by session availability

accepted.name: driver_dim
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  driver_id,
  driver_ref,
  number,
  code,
  forename,
  surname,
  dob,
  nationality,
  url,
  (COALESCE(forename, '') || CASE WHEN forename IS NOT NULL AND surname IS NOT NULL THEN ' ' ELSE '' END || COALESCE(surname, '')) AS full_name
FROM drivers
accepted.description: Canonical projection of drivers keeping original driver attributes and a full_name derived column. Use when joining driver info to results, lap times, standings, qualifying, and pit stops. | Use for: Resolve driver display name; Join driver attributes to results, lap times, pit stops, standings

accepted.name: constructor_dim
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  c.constructor_id,
  c.constructor_ref,
  c.name,
  c.nationality,
  c.url,
  ce.short_name AS short_name
FROM constructors c
LEFT JOIN constructors_ext ce USING (constructor_id)
accepted.description: Normalized constructors projection exposing canonical attributes and short_name if available in constructors_ext via LEFT JOIN. Useful for reports combining team metadata with results or standings. | Use for: Show constructor nationality and display name; Join constructor metadata to results, constructor_standings, constructor_results

accepted.name: race_results
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  r.result_id,
  r.race_id,
  r.driver_id,
  r.constructor_id,
  r.number,
  r.grid,
  r.position,
  r.position_text,
  r.position_order,
  r.points,
  r.laps,
  r.time,
  r.milliseconds,
  r.fastest_lap,
  r.rank,
  r.fastest_lap_time,
  r.fastest_lap_speed,
  r.status_id,
  d.driver_ref,
  d.forename,
  d.surname,
  d.number AS driver_number,
  c.constructor_ref,
  c.name AS constructor_name,
  race.name AS race_name,
  race.year,
  race.round
FROM results r
LEFT JOIN drivers d USING (driver_id)
LEFT JOIN constructors c USING (constructor_id)
LEFT JOIN races race USING (race_id)
accepted.description: Denormalized results per race-driver including driver and constructor attributes and race metadata. One row per results.result_id. Useful as the base for finish-position analyses, points aggregation, and joins to lap/pit data. | Use for: Who finished where in a race; Aggregate points by driver or constructor for a race or season; Filter results by driver/constructor/race attributes

accepted.name: lap_times_per_driver
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  race_id,
  driver_id,
  COUNT(*) AS lap_count,
  MIN(milliseconds) AS min_milliseconds,
  MAX(milliseconds) AS max_milliseconds,
  AVG(milliseconds) AS avg_milliseconds
FROM lap_times
GROUP BY race_id, driver_id
accepted.description: Aggregated lap time statistics per race and driver: count of laps, min/avg/max milliseconds. Useful for performance comparisons across drivers or races. | Use for: Compare drivers by average lap time in a race; Find drivers with fastest single lap in a race

accepted.name: pit_stops_per_driver
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  race_id,
  driver_id,
  COUNT(*) AS pit_stop_count,
  SUM(milliseconds) AS total_pit_milliseconds,
  AVG(milliseconds) AS avg_pit_milliseconds
FROM pit_stops
GROUP BY race_id, driver_id
accepted.description: Aggregated pit stop metrics per race and driver: number of stops and total/avg duration in milliseconds when available. Useful for pit strategy analysis and joins to results. | Use for: How many pit stops each driver made in a race; Relate pit stop time to finishing position

accepted.name: qualifying_grid
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  q.qualify_id,
  q.race_id,
  q.driver_id,
  q.constructor_id,
  q.number,
  q.position AS qualifying_position,
  q.q1,
  q.q2,
  q.q3,
  d.forename,
  d.surname,
  c.name AS constructor_name
FROM qualifying q
LEFT JOIN drivers d USING (driver_id)
LEFT JOIN constructors c USING (constructor_id)
accepted.description: Qualifying projections per race-driver including best qualifying position and Q1/Q2/Q3 times. Useful for comparing grid position to race results. | Use for: Analyze how qualifying position relates to race finish; List grid order for a race

accepted.name: driver_championship_rank
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  ds.driver_standings_id,
  ds.race_id,
  ds.driver_id,
  ds.points,
  ds.position,
  ds.position_text,
  ds.wins,
  RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY ds.race_id ORDER BY ds.points DESC) AS season_rank_by_points
FROM driver_standings ds
accepted.description: Windowed rank of drivers within each race snapshot based on driver_standings points. Exposes position and points; use to find top-N in standings at any race snapshot. | Use for: Top N drivers in championship after a given race; Compare official 'position' to computed rank by points

accepted.name: fastest_lap_rank_per_race
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  r.result_id,
  r.race_id,
  r.driver_id,
  r.fastest_lap,
  r.fastest_lap_time,
  r.fastest_lap_speed,
  r.milliseconds AS race_finish_milliseconds,
  RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY r.race_id ORDER BY r.fastest_lap) AS fastest_lap_rank
FROM results r
WHERE r.fastest_lap IS NOT NULL
accepted.description: Ranks drivers in a race by their fastest lap milliseconds (from results.fastest_lap_time via milliseconds where available). Exposes rank so callers can filter top performers. One row per result. | Use for: Who set the fastest lap in each race; Top fastest lap performers per race

accepted.name: circuits_with_summary
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  c.circuit_id,
  c.circuit_ref,
  c.name,
  c.location,
  c.country,
  c.lat,
  c.lng,
  c.alt,
  c.url,
  ce.last_race_year,
  ce.number_of_races
FROM circuits c
LEFT JOIN circuits_ext ce USING (circuit_id)
accepted.description: Circuits enriched with summary fields from circuits_ext when available (last_race_year, number_of_races). One row per circuit. | Use for: List circuits and their last active year; Map races to circuit coordinates

accepted.name: lap_times_running_stats
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  lt.race_id,
  lt.driver_id,
  lt.lap,
  lt.position,
  lt.time,
  lt.milliseconds,
  ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY lt.race_id, lt.driver_id ORDER BY lt.lap) AS lap_sequence,
  SUM(lt.milliseconds) OVER (PARTITION BY lt.race_id, lt.driver_id ORDER BY lt.lap ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) AS running_total_milliseconds
FROM lap_times lt
accepted.description: Per race-driver ordered lap times with a running count and running total milliseconds to support pace curves and running-average analyses. One row per lap (preserves lap grain). | Use for: Plot race pace per driver over laps; Compute moving average lap time per driver
